title: Give the page a clear outline
summary: Headings tell readers how a page is organised.
introduction: Headings tell readers how a page is organised. Your task: Add another h3 job under Jobs.
learningObjectives: Add another h3 job under Jobs.
Explain the example for give the page a clear outline

blocks.text: Headings tell readers how a page is organised. A screen reader can list headings to help someone move between topics.

Try runnable HTML here with a keyboard as well as a mouse. A screen reader is a tool that reads page information aloud. Test real pages with people and tools; one automated check cannot prove everything works.

blocks.code:
Our school garden

Plants

We grow beans.

Jobs

Watering

Water in the morning.
blocks.title: Give the page a clear outline

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `h1` names the whole page. `h2` starts the Plants and Jobs sections.
`h3` puts Watering inside the Jobs section rather than making it a new main section.

blocks.text: The page has one main title, two main sections and a smaller watering section.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Choose heading levels for their place in the outline. Use CSS to change size instead of skipping levels for appearance.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Add another h3 job under Jobs.
